question: What was the return rate for each product category last quarter?
sql: SELECT p.category, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(r.return_id) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM fact_order_items i JOIN fact_orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = i.product_key LEFT JOIN fact_returns r ON r.order_item_id = i.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' AND o.order_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30' GROUP BY p.category
notes: return rate per conventions: returned lines / lines on delivered orders, by order date; percent 1dp. Limit (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1): counting lines on delivered orders and lines on non-cancelled orders give identical rates for Jul-Sep (every order in that window is delivered), so this item cannot tell those two denominators apart; it does catch the return-date attribution and the quantity-weighted variants. precision=1 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: Top 5 beans by revenue in Bengaluru this year
sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(i.line_total_inr) AS revenue FROM fact_order_items i JOIN fact_orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = i.product_key WHERE p.category = 'beans' AND o.city = 'Bengaluru' AND o.order_date BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-10-31' AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY revenue DESC, p.product_name LIMIT 5
notes: product revenue = SUM(line_total_inr) excl cancelled; city = delivery city; tie-break by name. precision=0 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: Which product has the highest return rate? Only count products with at least 30 units sold.
sql: SELECT p.product_name, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(r.return_id) / COUNT(*), 1) AS rate FROM fact_order_items i JOIN fact_orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = i.product_key LEFT JOIN fact_returns r ON r.order_item_id = i.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 30 ORDER BY rate DESC, p.product_name LIMIT 1
notes: units = order lines on delivered orders, all time. Known pattern: GR-005 defect batch. Limit (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1): the top product is GR-005 under delivered, non-cancelled and all-lines denominators, so the name alone does not separate them; the rate (28.2 / 25.6 / 24.4) does, at 1 decimal. precision=1 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: By what percentage did revenue grow from fiscal Q1 to fiscal Q2 of FY2026-27?
sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (q2.r - q1.r) / q1.r, 1) FROM (SELECT SUM(o.total_inr) AS r FROM fact_orders o JOIN dim_date d ON d.full_date = o.order_date WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026-27' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1) q1, (SELECT SUM(o.total_inr) AS r FROM fact_orders o JOIN dim_date d ON d.full_date = o.order_date WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026-27' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 2) q2
notes: Q1 = Apr-Jun 2026, Q2 = Jul-Sep 2026; revenue = SUM(total_inr) excl cancelled; percent, 1 decimal. CHANGED (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1): was 'revenue for each fiscal quarter, oldest first' (revenue column only), which could not be scored without a label column; now one growth figure that needs the fiscal calendar. precision=1 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: On average, how many orders per day did we get on weekends versus weekdays last quarter?
sql: SELECT d.is_weekend, ROUND(COUNT(o.order_id)::numeric / COUNT(DISTINCT d.full_date), 1) FROM dim_date d LEFT JOIN fact_orders o ON o.order_date = d.full_date AND o.status <> 'cancelled' WHERE d.full_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30' GROUP BY d.is_weekend
notes: two rows (weekend, weekday); excl cancelled; 1 decimal. CHANGED (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1): gold keeps the is_weekend label column (was values only); the agent may return a boolean or a text label from label_map; swapped labels fail because rows must line up. precision=1 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: Of customers who ordered this year, what share ordered more than once, by signup channel?
sql: SELECT c.signup_channel, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.n > 1) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM (SELECT o.customer_key, COUNT(*) AS n FROM fact_orders o WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-10-31' AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_key) t JOIN dim_customer_safe c ON c.customer_key = t.customer_key GROUP BY c.signup_channel
notes: repeat = more than one non-cancelled order in FY2026-27 to date; percent 1dp. precision=1 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: Delivery tickets per 100 orders, by month
sql: SELECT t.m, ROUND(100.0 * t.n / o.n, 1) FROM (SELECT TO_CHAR(created_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS m, COUNT(*) AS n FROM fact_tickets WHERE category = 'delivery' GROUP BY 1) t JOIN (SELECT TO_CHAR(order_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS m, COUNT(*) AS n FROM fact_orders WHERE status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY 1) o ON o.m = t.m
notes: tickets by created month over non-cancelled orders by order month; 12 rows; Aug 2026 spike. precision=1 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: Gross margin in rupees by product category this year, biggest first
sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(i.line_total_inr - i.quantity * p.unit_cost_inr) AS margin FROM fact_order_items i JOIN fact_orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = i.product_key WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-10-31' AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY margin DESC, p.category
notes: margin = line_total_inr - quantity * unit_cost_inr; excl cancelled. precision=0 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: Revenue in October split between the Diwali run-up days and the other days
sql: SELECT COALESCE(d.festival = 'Diwali Run-up', false) AS diwali_runup, SUM(o.total_inr) FROM fact_orders o JOIN dim_date d ON d.full_date = o.order_date WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2026-10-01' AND '2026-10-31' AND o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY COALESCE(d.festival = 'Diwali Run-up', false)
notes: two rows (run-up 12-31 Oct, other 1-11 Oct); excl cancelled. CHANGED (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1): gold keeps the flag column (was values only); NULL festival days count as 'other'; label_map accepts text labels; swapped labels fail. precision=0 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).

question: Month-over-month growth in orders for the last 3 months
sql: SELECT m, ROUND(100.0 * (n - prev) / prev, 1) FROM (SELECT m, n, LAG(n) OVER (ORDER BY m) AS prev FROM (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)::date AS m, COUNT(*) AS n FROM fact_orders WHERE status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY 1) q) t WHERE m >= '2026-08-01' ORDER BY m
notes: last 3 months = Aug, Sep, Oct 2026, each vs the previous month; percent 1dp. precision=1 set (review 2026-11-10, before live run 1).
